2

4	
5	## Context

7	Every surface returns every prop the checker resolves, minus what a collapsed layer hides. 8	
9	The checker's cost follows what it converts, not what is shown. A whole-project `extract` of Chakra's own repository built 42 GB of `PropType` trees converting its style system (`shrink/chakra-memory.md`), and the only memory guard (`OnDemandConfig::max_rss_mib`, `crates/semantic/src/on_demand.rs:93`) reads the checker's arenas (`crates/semantic/src/checker.rs:169`), not the converter's heap, and only between requests (`on_demand.rs:643`).
10	
11	## Decision
12	
13	### A. Relevance decides what is shown, from evidence
14	
15	The owner's rules: returning all resolved props is useless for Storybook and agents; relevance decides what to show; it is derived from evidence, with no name lists; agent output is narrowed later.
16	
17	**Signals.** Each prop a component's props type reaches gets evidence from four places.
18	
19	- **The props type.** A member the props type declares itself is always shown. So is each key of `Pick<X, 'a' | 'b'>`, named on purpose; `Omit<X, 'k'>` says only that `k` is gone, nothing about the rest. A member that redeclares or narrows a base member is the component's own. A required member is shown (a story cannot render without it), and so is one with a `@default` tag or a destructuring default in the body (the component handles it). JSDoc and a literal-union type do not show a member on their own: as promoters they would list every documented member of a style system; they order the shown rows (open question 1).
20	- **Spreads in the body** (T1's `ComponentMapping::body`). `{...rest}` on a DOM tag passes the ambient DOM attributes: no evidence, ignored. A spread onto a component is one hop to that component's own non-ambient props, with the JSX tag resolved to the component by symbol and import (ADR 0027's identity, never the display name). An attribute set after the spread is fixed and subtracted; one set before it is an overridable default and kept; an attribute whose value is one of the component's own props adds nothing. A name in `reads` is shown when its source is not ambient.
21	- **Call sites.** The props consumers pass at JSX usages across the project (T1's `SourceData::jsx_usages`) and in stories' `args`, counted per component with a floor of `max(2, 20%)` of its sites. The baseline puts the cost at 0.30 (Mantine), 0.03 (Spectrum), 0.76 (shadcn) and 0.24 (antd) extra entries per component.
22	- **Unknown.** When `handed_on` is true, `reads` is incomplete (T1's contract), and the body says nothing: never guessed. 23	
24	**Ambient** is decided by where a member is declared, not by its name: a member `@types/react` declares (by declaring path, as `is_react_declared` in `crates/semantic/src/component.rs` recognizes React terminals), or one that reaches the component only through a spread onto a DOM tag. 25	
26	**Combination.** One function, `relevance::decide(&Evidence) -> Shown`, owns it, as `CollapseInheritedProps::collapses` owns collapsing; both lanes and every surface call it.
27	
28	- Shown as a row: own, picked, overriding, required, defaulted; a non-ambient member that is forwarded, read, or passed at the floor.
29	- Named in the layer's `used` list: an ambient member passed at the floor or read in the body.
30	- Left in a collapsed layer: everything else with complete evidence, even from a source today's rule lists (its source becomes a layer). A non-ambient member with unknown body evidence and no other signal is listed or collapsed as today.
31

33

35	
36	**Acceptance gate** (T5's metric, ported into the weekly by T4). Coverage counts a passed prop as visible when it is a row or in `used`. On the half the floor is `max(1, 20%)`, and only components with at least 6 sites are measured, so the gate does not test a stricter rule than the one shipped.
37	
38	- Coverage mean rises: shadcn 0.43 to at least 0.70; Mantine 0.86 to at least 0.88; antd 0.91 to at least 0.93; Spectrum stays at least 0.96.

43	
44	The owner asked for a queue. Its parts, against what exists:
45	
46	- **Item.** The props of one component that relevance will show, at one revision, not the whole component; collapsed members are listed by name and parent and never converted. New: the scheduler admits a background item only under a soft budget read from the allocator, holds background work above it, and stops the checker above the hard one, as `stop_past_bound` does.
51	- **Stream each result.** Exists: one `Delivery` per request (`types/semantic.rs:256`), and the reducer turns each settled key into a refresh (`lifecycle.ts:185-205`, invariants 1 to 6). New: a request of several keys delivers each key when converted. The CLI keeps one write: canonical JSON interns props across components (ADR 0009, 0018).
52	
53	Not determined: whether tsrs's memory allows the converter memo to live as long as a snapshot over a long session (ADR 0026 measured 98 to 246 MB over 150 edits without it); whether `mi_process_info` reads the same under the napi host; how far listing collapsed members without converting them lowers the 42 GB case, since the collapse PR collapses `SystemProperties` after conversion.

56	
57	- Output changes on every surface; the addon's default argTypes change again after the collapse PR. 59	- Call-site evidence makes a component's answer depend on other files. Watch and the kept answer must invalidate on a consumer's edit, and the per-component closure is still unknown (ADR 0026), so invalidation stays whole-project.

61	- Breaking for readers of `InheritedLayer` (schema 8).
62

64	
65	- **A fixed universal set** (`className`, `style`, `id`, `aria-*`, `data-*`, `ref` plus handlers): about the same 1 to 3 rows, but a name list.

A spread onto a component is one hop to that component's own non-ambient props, with the JSX tag resolved to the component by symbol and import (ADR 0027's identity, never the display name). An attribute set after the spread is fixed and subtracted; one set before it is an overridable default and kept; an attribute whose value is one of the component's own props adds nothing. A name in `reads` is shown when its source is not ambient.
- **Call sites.** The props consumers pass at JSX usages across the project (T1's `SourceData::jsx_usages`) and in stories' `args`, counted per component with a floor of `max(2, 20%)` of its sites. The baseline puts the cost at 0.30 (Mantine), 0.03 (Spectrum), 0.76 (shadcn) and 0.24 (antd) extra entries per component.

**Ambient** is decided by where a member is declared, not by its name: a member `@types/react` declares (by declaring path, as `is_react_declared` in `crates/semantic/src/component.rs` recognizes React terminals), or one that reaches the component only through a spread onto a DOM tag. **Combination.** One function, `relevance::decide(&Evidence) -> Shown`, owns it, as `CollapseInheritedProps::collapses` owns collapsing; both lanes and every surface call it.

- Shown as a row: own, picked, overriding, required, defaulted; a non-ambient member that is forwarded, read, or passed at the floor.
- Named in the layer's `used` list: an ambient member passed at the floor or read in the body.
- Left in a collapsed layer: everything else with complete evidence, even from a source today's rule lists (its source becomes a layer). A non-ambient member with unknown body evidence and no other signal is listed or collapsed as today.

**Output.** A collapsed `InheritedLayer` (`crates/core/src/types/output.rs:83`) gains `used`: the names of its members that evidence put forward, written once as a name list (ADR 0018), not as typed rows. Universal props such as `className`, `style` and `id` cost a name each instead of a row each. A `React.ComponentProps<"el">` layer also gets its `members`, so a reader can check `used` against it. No per-prop flag in this ADR: the row/layer split already says shown or not, and why a row is shown is for the agent output, deferred. `SCHEMA_VERSION` goes from 7 to 8 (ADR 0017), with the RDT view, the JSON schema, `binding.d.ts` and a changeset.

**Consumers.** The Storybook addon makes argTypes from rows, then one name-only row per `used` name with the layer as its category; an option (`relevance: 'all'`) asks for the expanded output, which is today's `collapseInheritedProps: 'none'`. CLI JSON and TOON carry the same output. Agent output keeps its current form until the agent flow is narrowed.

**Acceptance gate** (T5's metric, ported into the weekly by T4). Coverage counts a passed prop as visible when it is a row or in `used`. Call-site evidence is computed from half of the files (by path hash) and coverage is measured on the other half, so the gate does not pass by construction. On the half the floor is `max(1, 20%)`, and only components with at least 6 sites are measured, so the gate does not test a stricter rule than the one shipped.

The owner asked for a queue. Its parts, against what exists:

- **Item.** The props of one component that relevance will show, at one revision, not the whole component; collapsed members are listed by name and parent and never converted. Exists: `SemanticTarget::react_wanted` and `described` (`crates/core/src/types/semantic.rs:169-175`) already narrow what one target converts. New: a `shown` set from `relevance::decide`.
- **Priority classes**, on-screen > neighbouring stories > background fill. Exists: two (`Priority::Interactive` and `Background`, `types/semantic.rs:221`), two lanes with a starvation bound and raising (`Queue`, `on_demand.rs:150-199`, `INTERACTIVE_STREAK` 4), a raise when an on-screen request joins a queued one (`pipeline/semantic_hook.rs:256`). The addon's prefetch queue holds the next `prefetchStories - 1` stories, replaced on every selection (`packages/storybook/src/background.ts:39`, `preset.ts:150`, `prefetch.ts:32`), one story at a time (`background.ts:81-89`), and asks at `Background` (`pipeline/watch.rs:464`). New: a third class, `Neighbour`, between them.

Missing: nothing reaches `OnDemand`'s queue, which has no cancel, so requests nobody waits for still run. New: a request carries a cancel token tripped by an edit or by the navigation that replaced it, dropped when taken. Raising a request clears its token: an on-screen request that joined a queued prefetch (`Found::Joined`, `semantic_hook.rs:256`) is waited for, so a navigation never cancels it; and preemption between components of one request (a tsrs call cannot be interrupted).
